content: 1. Etravirine and Aripiprazole: Etravirine reduces the plasma levels and therapeutic effects of aripiprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended when these drugs are co-administered. 2. Etravirine and Armodafinil: Armodafinil increases etravirine levels via CYP2C19 inhibition but decreases etravirine levels through CYP3A4 induction. Etravirine, in turn, reduces armodafinil levels by inducing CYP3A4. Monitor closely due to these bidirectional interactions. 3. Etravirine and Artemether/Lumefantrine: Etravirine significantly reduces the levels of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to a loss of antimalarial efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 4. Etravirine and Atazanavir: Atazanavir increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, while etravirine decreases atazanavir levels. However, this interaction is not clinically significant when atazanavir is combined with ritonavir. No dose adjustments are necessary. 5. Etravirine and Atidarsagene Autotemcel: Antiretroviral therapy (ART), including etravirine, may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. ART should be discontinued at least one month before cell mobilization and during the elimination period of the drugs. 6. Etravirine and Atogepant: Etravirine reduces atogepant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the atogepant dose to 30 mg or 60 mg daily when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 7. Etravirine and Atorvastatin: Etravirine decreases atorvastatin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor lipid levels and adjust atorvastatin dosage as needed. 8. Etravirine and Avanafil: Etravirine reduces avanafil levels via CYP3A4 induction, potentially decreasing its efficacy in treating erectile dysfunction. Monitor patient response closely. 9. Etravirine and Avapritinib: Etravirine decreases avapritinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Etravirine and Axitinib: Etravirine reduces axitinib levels through CYP3A4 induction, potentially compromising its therapeutic efficacy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 11. Etravirine and Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Etravirine decreases the levels of these drugs by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and use caution. 12. Etravirine and Bedaquiline: Etravirine reduces bedaquiline levels via CYP3A4 induction, potentially leading to reduced therapeutic efficacy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 13. Etravirine and Belumosudil: Etravirine decreases belumosudil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase the belumosudil dose to 200 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 14. Etravirine and Belzutifan: Belzutifan reduces etravirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. If co-administration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 15. Etravirine and Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Etravirine decreases hydrocodone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Discontinuation of CYP3A4 inducers may lead to increased hydrocodone levels, risking respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 16. Etravirine and Betibeglogene Autotemcel: ART, including etravirine, may interfere with the manufacturing of betibeglogene autotemcel. ART should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and during the elimination period of the drugs. 17. Etravirine and Betrixaban: Etravirine increases betrixaban levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp). Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, followed by 40 mg daily, when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 18. Etravirine and Bexarotene: Etravirine reduces bexarotene levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor closely and use caution. 19. Etravirine and Bortezomib: Bortezomib increases etravirine levels via CYP2C19 inhibition, while etravirine reduces bortezomib levels through CYP3A4 induction. Monitor closely due to these bidirectional interactions. 20. Etravirine and Bosentan: Bosentan reduces etravirine levels via CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 induction. Etravirine also affects bosentan levels. Monitor closely, as the clinical significance is unknown. 21. Etravirine and Bosutinib: Etravirine reduces bosutinib levels via CYP3A4 induction, potentially decreasing its efficacy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 22. Etravirine and Brexpiprazole: Etravirine reduces brexpiprazole levels via CYP3A4 induction. Double the brexpiprazole dose over 1–2 weeks if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 23. Etravirine and Brigatinib: Etravirine reduces brigatinib levels via CYP3A4 induction, potentially compromising its efficacy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 24. Etravirine and Bromocriptine: Etravirine reduces bromocriptine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor closely and use caution. 25. Etravirine and Budesonide: Etravirine reduces budesonide levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor closely and use caution. 26. Etravirine and Buprenorphine: Etravirine reduces buprenorphine levels (including buccal, subdermal, transdermal, and long-acting injection forms) via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for withdrawal symptoms and adjust therapy as needed. 27. Etravirine and Buspirone: Etravirine reduces buspirone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor closely and use caution. 28. Etravirine and Butabarbital/Butalbital: These drugs reduce etravirine levels via CYP2C19, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 induction. Monitor closely and use caution. 29. Etravirine and Cabazitaxel: Etravirine reduces cabazitaxel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 30. Etravirine and Cabozantinib: Etravirine reduces cabozantinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or increase the cabozantinib dose as clinically appropriate. 31. Etravirine and Calcifediol/Calcitriol: Etravirine reduces the levels of these drugs via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 32. Etravirine and Cannabidiol: Etravirine affects cannabidiol levels through CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Cannabidiol may also inhibit CYP2C9 activity. Monitor closely and adjust doses as needed. 33. Etravirine and Capivasertib: Etravirine reduces capivasertib levels via CYP3A4 induction, potentially reducing efficacy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 34. Etravirine and Capmatinib: Etravirine reduces capmatinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor closely and use caution. 35. Etravirine and Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine reduces etravirine levels via CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 induction, potentially leading to virologic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 36. Etravirine and Cariprazine: Etravirine reduces cariprazine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the unclear net effect on cariprazine exposure. 37. Etravirine and Carvedilol: Etravirine increases carvedilol levels via CYP2C9/10 inhibition. Monitor closely and use caution. 38. Etravirine and Celecoxib: Etravirine increases celecoxib levels via CYP2C9/10 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Etravirine and Cenobamate: Cenobamate affects etravirine levels through CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Adjust doses of CYP2C19 substrates as clinically appropriate. 40. Etravirine and Ceritinib: Etravirine reduces ceritinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 41. Etravirine and Cevimeline: Etravirine reduces cevimeline levels via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unknown. 42. Etravirine and Chlordiazepoxide: Etravirine reduces chlordiazepoxide levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor closely and use caution. 43. Etravirine and Cilostazol: Etravirine reduces cilostazol levels via CYP3A4 induction but increases its toxicity via CYP2C19 inhibition. Consider dose reduction of cilostazol. 44. Etravirine and Cimetidine: Cimetidine increases etravirine levels via CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely and use caution.
